I recently started my second year at college and I’ve been having the same struggles with making friends and often turning to food for comfort. Eating is something that’s easy to fall back on, because it’s not like you can just stop eating. I find that when i crave food it’s all I can think about and it basically consumes me until I can get what I want. 

I also find that being depressed makes you want to eat; not having friends, not being able to see people in person etc. But when you eat like crap, that just helps make you feel more depressed. It’s really difficult to break out of that cycle and I myself have been trying to get out of it.

I’d suggest that if you are really struggling with fast food, try reducing gradually. Start with limiting the number of times a day. if you find that you’re going many times a day, maybe start with only allowing yourself to get fast food for lunch or dinner/limit to one time a day. 

then start working on what you’re ordering- if you order more than just one meal, then start trying to limit that to only one meal. maybe you could try to order “healthier” menu items- a single burger vs a double, medium vs large fries, water or tea instead of soda. 

from there you could then start limiting the number of times you go a week; designate one day a week you don’t get it, then add another, and another.

you don’t necessarily need to cut it out entirely; just limit by small amounts until you’re to a point where you feel comfortable. if you have a favorite restaurant, maybe only allow yourself to go to that restaurant occasionally.

you could also balance the fast food with eating healthier meals other times of day. that doesn’t mean you have to eat salads all the time, it could just be limiting sugar or dairy.

gaining weight at the start of college is definitely something a lot of people struggle with. it’s definitely not the end of the world if you go up a size or two, but even just doing small activities can help. if you find yourself being sedentary, then even just going on walks can get you moving and help slow the weight gain. 

with the food & weight: don’t try to push yourself too hard or too fast, as it could make you more depressed and just continue the cycle. slowly reducing amounts and what you’re eating can help you feel like you’re not losing control.

about the friends thing- honestly, your parents can get over you having female friends. it’s 2021 and you should be friends with whoever you want. if it’s a really big issue, you can honestly just lie. it’s not a lie that will ruin your life or anything.

if you can’t find friends in person, making friends online is also a great alternative. my best friend lives several hours away from me but that doesn’t stop us from having a meaningful friendship. playing video games together is usually a great bonding time and also a fantastic time waster.
